headline: Adani Group plans $120 billion capex, wins major power supply contract
summary: Adani Group outlines a massive $120 billion 5-6 year capex plan, while subsidiary AESL secures a major 1,750 MW renewable energy contract in West Bengal. Adani Airports raises $300 million to expand non-aero infrastructure, and CRISIL upgrades Adani Power's credit rating to AA+.

stories.what: Adani Group plans to invest over $120 billion over the next 5-6 years across infrastructure, energy, and data centres. Reported by Business Standard via a Jefferies research note, the group aims to keep its net debt below 3.5 times EBITDA during this expansion.
stories.why: Demonstrates the group's aggressive expansion strategy across core verticals while maintaining leverage discipline.
stories.watch: Execution timelines for data centres under AdaniConneX
stories.title: Adani Group planning $120 bn in capex over next 5-6 years: Jefferies

stories.what: Powerpulse Trading Solutions, a subsidiary of Adani Energy Solutions Limited, received a Letter of Award from WBSEDCL to supply 1,750 MW of round-the-clock renewable energy for 25 years starting July 1, 2028. The contract includes a 750 MW greenshoe option.
stories.why: Secures long-term cash flow predictability and expands the group's presence in round-the-clock clean energy contracts.
stories.watch: Whether WBSEDCL exercises the 750 MW greenshoe option
stories.title: AESL arm secures 1,750 MW RE-RTC supply contract from WBSEDCL

stories.what: Adani Airport Holdings signed a binding agreement to raise ₹2,790 crore ($300 million) by selling up to a 1.55% stake to 360 ONE Asset. The funds will be used to develop non-aeronautical commercial infrastructure such as city-side hotels.
stories.why: Drives higher margin, non-regulated commercial revenue growth across airport properties.
stories.watch: Commercial monetization milestones for airport real estate
stories.title: Adani Airports chases fast-growing non-aero revenues with latest $300-mn fund raise

stories.what: CRISIL upgraded Adani Power's credit rating to CRISIL AA+/Stable from CRISIL AA/Stable covering bank loans and NCD facilities worth ₹90,500 crore. The upgrade is attributed to a strong business profile and a high share of power purchase agreements.
stories.why: Lowers borrowing costs and signals improving balance sheet strength for thermal assets.
stories.watch: Impact on future debt refinancing costs
stories.title: CRISIL upgrades Adani Power's rating to AA+/Stable

stories.why: Highlights regulatory and environmental compliance friction risk in execution of hydro assets.
stories.watch: MPCB response to the company's clarification on support facilities
stories.title: Adani’s Tarali project: The dispute over its cost and wildlife fee

stories.watch: Ramp up of domestic copper processing volume
stories.title: Adani signs 3-year copper supply deal with Attero: Report

concept.explain: A greenshoe option is a provision in a contract or offer that allows the issuer or seller to expand the transaction size beyond the initial target. In today's power deal, WBSEDCL secured 1,750 MW of power with an option to purchase an extra 750 MW under identical terms. For infrastructure players, it provides a built-in upside to scale revenues without re-bidding.

question.q: Why is Adani Airports raising private equity for non-aeronautical infrastructure instead of core airport operations?
question.a: Aeronautical revenues are heavily regulated based on cost-plus tariffs set by regulators. Non-aeronautical assets like city-side hotels, retail, and duty-free offer unregulated, higher-margin growth, making equity funding attractive for rapid commercial development.

headline: Adani expands across airports, green power, defense, and power transmission infrastructure.
summary: Adani Airport Holdings raised $300 million to boost non-aero revenues, while Adani Energy Solutions secured major renewable supply and transmission contracts in West Bengal and Bihar. Meanwhile, Adani Power received a CRISIL credit rating upgrade, and Adani Defence successfully demonstrated its Bagheera AT1 missile system in Pokhran.

stories.what: Adani Airport Holdings Limited raised ₹2,790 crore ($300 million) in primary equity from 360 ONE Asset, bringing its total equity raise to date to approximately $1.35 billion (₹12,615 crore). 360 ONE Asset will acquire up to a 1.55% stake in the entity.
stories.why: The capital will be deployed to accelerate the development of city-side infrastructure such as hotels to expand high-margin non-aeronautical revenue streams.
stories.watch: Execution speed of city-side real estate buildouts across its airport portfolio.
stories.title: Adani Airports raises ~USD 300 million primary equity from 360 ONE Asset

stories.what: Powerpulse Trading Solutions Limited, a subsidiary of Adani Energy Solutions, secured a Letter of Award from WBSEDCL for supplying 1,750 MW of round-the-clock renewable energy over 25 years. The award includes a 750 MW greenshoe option that could raise total capacity to 2,500 MW, with initial supply starting July 1, 2028.
stories.why: Long-term round-the-clock renewable contracts guarantee stable, long-dated cash flows and strengthen the group's position in complex green power trading.
stories.watch: Whether WBSEDCL exercises the 750 MW greenshoe option prior to 2029.
stories.title: AESL arm secures 1,750 MW RE-RTC supply contract from WBSEDCL

stories.what: Adani Energy Solutions secured a tariff-based competitive bidding transmission project in Bihar linked to evacuating power from the 2,400 MW Pirpainti Ultra Super Critical Thermal Power Plant. The asset is expected to generate about ₹500 crore in annual tariff revenue, with a target completion date of Q4 2028.
stories.why: Expands AESL's portfolio of annuity-like regulated tariff power transmission assets across strategic regional corridors.
stories.title: Adani Energy Solutions Secures Rs 500 Cr Bihar Transmission Project

stories.what: CRISIL upgraded Adani Power Limited's credit rating to CRISIL AA+/Stable from CRISIL AA/Stable. The rating upgrade covers enhanced bank loan facilities and non-convertible debentures totaling ₹90,500 crore.
stories.why: Reflects a strengthened balance sheet, lower financial risk profile, and robust cash flows driven by a high share of long-term power purchase agreements.
stories.watch: Impact of lower borrowing costs on future capital expenditure refinancing.
stories.title: CRISIL upgrades Adani Power's rating to AA+/Stable

According to a Jefferies research note, the group intends to keep its net debt below 3.5 times EBITDA, while AdaniConneX reports a 1.2 GW data center order book.
stories.why: Confirms aggressive long-term infrastructure scaling while maintaining strict leverage guardrails to reassure capital markets.

stories.why: Demonstrates progress in building domestic military equipment capabilities under India's defense indigenization push.
stories.watch: Potential order conversion from the Indian Armed Forces following NCNC trials.

concept.explain: Non-aeronautical revenue refers to income generated by airport operators from non-flight activities such as retail leases, duty-free shopping, parking fees, advertising, and city-side real estate development like hotels. Unlike regulated aeronautical tariffs charged to airlines, non-aero income yields significantly higher margins and is less sensitive to flight volume fluctuations. Building out robust non-aero infrastructure, as seen in Adani Airports' latest $300 million fundraise, optimizes land utilization and boosts overall airport equity valuations.

question.q: Why is Adani Airports diluting equity at the subsidiary level to fund non-aeronautical infrastructure instead of relying purely on debt?
question.a: Raising primary equity from strategic investors like 360 ONE Asset keeps leverage ratios manageable while capital-intensive city-side real estate projects are under construction. Non-aeronautical assets like hotels and retail hubs have longer gestation periods before cash flow generation, making low-cost equity funding safer for balance sheet health than loading debt onto the parent company.
